questions.knowledge_point: Using Integration by Parts to Compute an Integral Containing an Arbitrary Logarithm
questions.worked_solution:
We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining $u$ and ${v}^{′},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}u={log}_{3}⁡(x)\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡3} \\ {v}^{′}=16{x}^{3}\, & ⟹\,v=\int 16{x}^{3}\,\text{d}x=4{x}^{4}\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 16{x}^{3}{log}_{3}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x & =\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={log}_{3}⁡(x)(4{x}^{4})-\int \frac{4{x}^{4}}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\,\text{d}x \\  & =4{x}^{4}{log}_{3}⁡(x)-\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\int 4{x}^{3}\,\text{d}x \\  & =4{x}^{4}{log}_{3}⁡(x)-\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\cdot {x}^{4}+C \\  & =\frac{4{x}^{4}\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}-\frac{{x}^{4}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}+C \\  & =\frac{{x}^{4}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}(4\operatorname{ln}⁡x-1)+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C$ is an integral constant.

Note that in the above calculation we used the change of base formula ${log}_{3}⁡x=\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}.$

We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining $u$ and ${v}^{′},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}u={log}_{2}⁡(x)\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡2} \\ {v}^{′}=25{x}^{4}\, & ⟹\,v=\int 25{x}^{4}\,\text{d}x=5{x}^{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 25{x}^{4}{log}_{2}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x & =\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={log}_{2}⁡(x)(5{x}^{5})-\int \frac{5{x}^{5}}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =5{x}^{5}{log}_{2}⁡(x)-\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}\int 5{x}^{4}\,\text{d}x \\  & =5{x}^{5}{log}_{2}⁡(x)-\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}\cdot {x}^{5}+C \\  & =\frac{5{x}^{5}\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}-\frac{{x}^{5}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}+C \\  & =\frac{{x}^{5}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}(5\operatorname{ln}⁡x-1)+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C$ is an integral constant.

Note that in the above calculation we used the change of base formula ${log}_{2}⁡x=\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}.$

questions.knowledge_point: Using Integration by Parts to Compute an Integral Containing a Single Logarithmic Factor
questions.worked_solution:
First, we write the integral as

$$
\int 2\operatorname{ln}⁡4x\,\text{d}x=2\int \operatorname{ln}⁡4x\cdot 1\,\text{d}x.
$$

 

We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining $u$ and ${v}^{′},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}u=\operatorname{ln}⁡(4x)\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{1}{x} \\ {v}^{′}=1\, & ⟹\,v=\int \,\text{d}x=x\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}2\int \operatorname{ln}⁡(4x)\,\text{d}x & =2\int u\,{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =2[uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x] \\  & =2[\operatorname{ln}⁡(4x)\cdot x-\int x\cdot \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x] \\  & =2[x\operatorname{ln}⁡(4x)-\int \,\text{d}x] \\  & =2x\operatorname{ln}⁡(4x)-2x+C \\  & =2x(\operatorname{ln}⁡(4x)-1)+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C$ is an integral constant.

questions.knowledge_point: Using Integration by Parts to Compute an Integral Containing a Single Logarithmic Factor
questions.worked_solution:
First, we write the integral as

$$
\int \operatorname{ln}⁡(x-3)\,\text{d}x=\int \operatorname{ln}⁡(x-3)\cdot 1\cdot \text{d}x.
$$

 

We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining $u$ and ${v}^{′},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}u=\operatorname{ln}⁡(x-3)\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{1}{x-3} \\ {v}^{′}=1\, & ⟹\,v=\int \,\text{d}x=x\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \operatorname{ln}⁡(x-3)\,\text{d}x & =\int u\,{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(x-3)\cdot x-\int x\cdot \frac{1}{x-3}\,\text{d}x \\  & =x\operatorname{ln}⁡(x-3)-\int \frac{x}{x-3}\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use a substitution $x-3=u,$ thus $x=u+3$ and $\text{d}x=\text{d}u.$ Hence,

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \operatorname{ln}⁡(x-3)\,\text{d}x & =x\operatorname{ln}⁡(x-3)-\int \frac{x}{x-3}\,\text{d}x \\  & =x\operatorname{ln}⁡(x-3)-\int \frac{u+3}{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =x\operatorname{ln}⁡(x-3)-\int \,\text{d}u-3\int \frac{\text{d}u}{u} \\  & =x\operatorname{ln}⁡(x-3)-u-3\operatorname{ln}⁡u+D \\  & =x\operatorname{ln}⁡(x-3)-(x-3)-3\operatorname{ln}⁡(x-3)+D \\  & =x\operatorname{ln}⁡(x-3)-3\operatorname{ln}⁡(x-3)-x+3+D \\  & =(x-3)\operatorname{ln}⁡(x-3)-x+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C=D+3$ is an integral constant.

questions.knowledge_point: Using Integration by Parts to Compute an Integral Containing a Single Logarithmic Factor
questions.worked_solution:
First, we write the integral as

$$
{\int }_{1/8}^{{e}^{3}/8}{log}_{3}⁡(8x)\,\text{d}x={\int }_{1/8}^{{e}^{3}/8}{log}_{3}⁡(8x)\cdot 1\cdot \text{d}x.
$$

 

We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining $u$ and ${v}^{′},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}u={log}_{3}⁡(8x)\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)} \\ {v}^{′}=1\, & ⟹\,v=\int 1\cdot \,dx=x\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1/8}^{{e}^{3}/8}{log}_{3}⁡(8x)\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{1/8}^{{e}^{3}/8}u{v}^{′}\text{d}x \\  & =uv{|}_{1/8}^{{e}^{3}/8}-{\int }_{1/8}^{{e}^{3}/8}v{u}^{′}\text{d}x \\  & ={log}_{3}⁡(8x)\,(x){|}_{1/8}^{{e}^{3}/8}-{\int }_{1/8}^{{e}^{3}/8}x(\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)})\,\text{d}x \\  & =[{log}_{3}⁡(8\cdot \frac{{e}^{3}}{8})\,(\frac{{e}^{3}}{8})-{log}_{3}⁡(8\cdot \frac{1}{8})\,(\frac{1}{8})]-\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)}{\int }_{1/8}^{{e}^{3}/8}\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{{e}^{3}}{8}{log}_{3}⁡({e}^{3})-\frac{1}{8}{log}_{3}⁡(1)-\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)}x{|}_{1/8}^{{e}^{3}/8} \\  & =\frac{{e}^{3}}{8}\cdot \frac{3}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)}-\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)}(\frac{{e}^{3}}{8}-\frac{1}{8}) \\  & =\frac{1}{8\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)}(2{e}^{3}+1).\end{aligned}
$$
